content.title: Trader Joe's eligible shoppers can claim class action settlement money
content.text: April 16, 2026, 12:32 p.m. ETShop at Trader Joe's? Eligible shoppers may be able to get a payout as part of a $7.4 million class action settlement money.Customers who made a purchase with a credit or debit card between March 5, 2019, and July 19, 2019, may be eligible to claim an estimated $102.45. Earlier this year, Trader Joe's agreed to settle a class action lawsuit filed in 2019 that alleged the company violated the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions (FACTA) act.According to court filings, it was alleged certain Trader Joe's stores printed receipts that displayed both the first six and last four digits of customers' card numbers, making them more susceptible to increased risk of identity theft.Trader Joe's denied all allegations and any wrongdoing or liability but agreed to settle the case to avoid further court proceedings. No customers have reported identity theft based on the allegations of the suit, Trader Joe's said.Are you eligible for a payout? Here's what to know about the settlement and how to find out if you are eligible to file a claim.What is the Trader Joe's class action settlement about?If you shopped at Trader Joe's and swiped your debit or credit card between March 5, 2019, and July 19, 2019, you may be in line for a $102.45 cash out. The grocery store, with several locations in New Jersey and the Mid-Atlantic region, has finalized a $7.4 million settlement to resolve a class action lawsuit over privacy concerns.The lawsuits stems from alleged violations of the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions (FACTA) act. The claim alleges several Trader Joe's locations issued receipts during a specific time window in 2019 that revealed sensitive data, specifically the first six and last four digits of customers' debit or credit cards. While it was exposed as a major risk, Trader Joe's has maintained its innocence, opting to settle the case instead of going through the costs and time of litigation.Who is eligible for cash in the Trader Joe's settlement?Not every Trader Joe's shopping trip in 2019 qualifies for the $102.45 payout. To be considered eligible for the money, you must meet the following requirements:You used your own debit or credit cards for a purchase at a Trader Joe's between March 5, 2019, and July, 19, 2019.You were issued a receipt where your first six and last four digits of your card number were incorrectly printed on it.You must be the primary account holder of the card used during that transaction.Not sure if you are eligible? Head to the Trader Joe's settlement website or call the settlement hotline at 1-888-444-7415. You can write a letter to the claim's administrator through the USPS:Keim v. Trader Joe’s Co. Settlement AdministratorP.O. Box 301134Los Angeles, CA 90030-1134How much money could I get?Eligible class members will receive a share of the $7.4 settlement, estimated to be about $102.45. However, the final amount is not fixed since it depends on the number of valid claims filed and deductions in settlement administration costs, such as attorney fees. The few people who apply for a claim, the larger each payout becomes.How to file a claim in the Trader Joe's settlementTrader Joe's customers who think they are eligible for money from the settlement can submit a claim now on the Trader Joe's settlement website. You have until June 9. Those with a Class ID number can submit their settlement forms by mail.When will I receive my payment?The timeline of the payout is tied to the court's final approval, with a hearing scheduled on Aug. 10, 2026. Once approved, there could be appeals and resolving them could take some time (up to a year). Updated information will be posted on the settlement website: Keim v. Trader Joe’s Company.Lori Comstock is a New Jersey-based news reporter covering trending news with USA TODAY Network's Mid-Atlantic Connect Team. She covers news in the Northeast, including New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Washington DC, Maryland, and Virginia. Reach her at LComstock@usatodayco.com.
